runtime_status.purpose: Show the intended shape of a future comparative analysis output before enabling runtime experiment execution.

research_alignment.dissertation_focus: Delay propagation in dynamic field operations.
research_alignment.main_question: Given a scenario class and a delay profile, which re-planning policy gives the best trade-off among performance, robustness, stability, feasibility, service quality, and computational cost?
research_alignment.scope_note: This sample keeps the academic focus on delays while leaving the platform extensible to new requests, cancellations, priority changes, and other operational disruptions.

comparison_unit.pairing_rule: Every candidate policy must be evaluated on the same instance, technician set, time horizon, initial schedule, perturbation script, and random seed.

candidate_policies.description: Keep the original schedule and only measure the consequences of delay propagation.
Trigger re-planning only when accumulated delay exceeds a defined threshold.
Re-plan at fixed decision epochs using the current state of the day.
Use an OR-Tools backed adapter for future VRP/TRSP/WSRP re-optimization experiments.
Optional MIP-backed comparison path, not required by the platform baseline.

sample_results.interpretation: Stable but weak under delay propagation because it absorbs delays without corrective action.
Better service recovery with moderate schedule disruption and low computational cost.
Competitive but may introduce unnecessary schedule changes when delays are localized.
Best sample service recovery, but with higher computational cost and more route changes.

statistical_analysis_plan.design: paired repeated experiment over the same scenario seeds
statistical_analysis_plan.primary_test: Friedman test or repeated-measures alternative depending on distributional assumptions
post_hoc_tests: paired Wilcoxon signed-rank tests with correction

sample_ranking.reason: Best sample service recovery under moderate delay propagation, with acceptable but higher computational cost.
Strong practical trade-off with low runtime and moderate stability loss.
Useful future baseline, but may overreact when delay propagation is localized.
Important baseline, but weak operational performance when delays propagate.

decision_framework_output.recommendation_logic: Although OR-Tools backed re-optimization has the best sample performance, threshold-based re-planning is the recommended practical policy for this sample because it gives a strong balance among service recovery, route stability, implementation simplicity, and computational cost.
decision_framework_output.future_framework_goal: Convert repeated comparative results into a reproducible rule or decision method for selecting re-planning policies by scenario class.

quality_requirements: Never rank policies from a single run.
Always compare candidate policies on paired scenarios.
Always report service, stability, feasibility, robustness, and computational cost trade-offs.
Always separate current implemented baselines from future solver-backed methods.
Always state that sample values are placeholders until generated by the experimental pipeline.
safety_requirements: The browser must not execute solvers.
The browser must not start experiments.
The browser must not mutate schedules.
The sample must not be described as a real experiment result.
Solver-backed policies must remain future integration items until actual execution infrastructure exists.
conservative_note: This file is a static read-only sample. It documents the intended comparative analysis output shape. It does not prove that any policy is superior, does not execute OR-Tools or Gurobi, and does not represent real experimental evidence yet.
